principles: Preserve existing gate semantics and fail-closed behavior.
Improve operator recovery only where a verified ambiguity exists.
Use host-neutral lattice wording instead of host-specific shortcuts unless the command is truly adapter-specific.
Keep each change testable through existing smoke surfaces.
drivers: Operators need actionable next commands when a gate failure is expected but recoverable.
Timeout and stale evidence failures should be distinguishable from logical test failures.
Delivery-check provenance and owner lease safety must remain explicit.

options.name: A: Targeted diagnostics and narrow alias suggestions
pros: Small diff with low blast radius
Directly addresses the verified recovery confusion
cons: Does not add full owner_status or owner_takeover command family
Does not infer historical timeout durations automatically

options.name: B: Add new recovery commands for owner, timeout tuning, and delivery fallback
pros: Could provide a richer recovery surface
cons: Larger design surface for a small verified issue
Higher risk of weakening reviewer/owner authority boundaries
Would require more docs and gate-policy work before it is safe

chosen: A: Targeted diagnostics and narrow alias suggestions
rationale: The verified issue is unclear recovery UX, not broken gate logic. Targeted diagnostics solve the immediate correctness problem while preserving lifecycle, reviewer, and owner lease semantics.

preMortem.scenario: A timeout hint accidentally makes timed-out validation look like a passing optional warning.
preMortem.trigger: The renderer adds recovery text but changes status/allPass or failure wording.
preMortem.consequence: A story could be advanced despite incomplete validation.
preMortem.mitigation: Only append detail text when result.timedOut is true; leave command code, timedOut, requiredFailures, status, and allPass logic unchanged and smoke-test failure status.

preMortem.scenario: Delivery fallback text encourages the main agent to write delivery_check_set as itself.
preMortem.trigger: The hint says manual fallback without naming reviewer actor/provenance requirements.
preMortem.consequence: The DONE artifact loses independent reviewer meaning even though the hash is valid.
preMortem.mitigation: Write the hint as a boundary: fallback is only compliant when executed under koala-review-delivery provenance or by rerunning the reviewer, never as main-agent self-review.

preMortem.scenario: Codex namespace compatibility broadens into a second command namespace with divergent semantics.
preMortem.trigger: Adding aliases for many codex-prefixed commands instead of the known core-command mistake.
preMortem.consequence: Docs and CLI behavior drift; host-neutral command model weakens.
preMortem.mitigation: Add only explicit guidance/aliases for known core commands or unknown-command suggestions; keep codex verify/doctor as adapter-specific.
